name: data and storage
owns: where state actually lives: relational, document, key value, queue, cache, search, object storage, and the paths in and out
why_in_D: An application is a thin decision layer over a store. Whenever the store accepts something the application did not intend, the application's rules stop mattering. Query languages are Turing-adjacent, document stores accept shapes nobody declared, and the export path is usually the widest read in the system.

factors.name: query language injection surface
factors.def: which positions in a query can carry user input without parameter binding
factors.observable: a clause altered by input while the query still returns rows

factors.name: parameter binding completeness
factors.def: whether identifiers, order clauses and limits are bound like values
factors.observable: injection through a position the builder treats as structure

factors.name: stacked query support
factors.def: whether the driver allows multiple statements per call
factors.observable: a second statement executed after the first

factors.name: error verbosity on query failure
factors.def: how much of the query and the schema reaches the client
factors.observable: query text or column names in a response

factors.name: boolean and time based inference viability
factors.def: whether a blind oracle is available through response difference or delay
factors.observable: a conditional delay correlated with a guessed predicate

factors.name: out of band channel availability
factors.def: whether the store can be made to make a network request or write a file
factors.observable: an outbound request triggered by a query

factors.name: second order input storage
factors.def: whether input is stored and later reused in a sensitive position without reencoding
factors.observable: an effect appearing on a later read rather than the write

factors.name: NoSQL operator injection
factors.def: whether a client supplied object can become a query operator rather than a value
factors.observable: a filter widened by a nested object in a parameter

factors.name: NoSQL type coercion in comparison
factors.def: whether a string can match a numeric or boolean field by coercion
factors.observable: a record returned for the wrong type

factors.name: document schema enforcement
factors.def: whether the store validates shape or accepts any document
factors.observable: an undeclared field persisted

factors.name: JSON path and expression injection
factors.def: whether a path or expression in a query can be influenced by input
factors.observable: a field read that the caller should not reach

factors.name: search engine query syntax exposure
factors.def: whether the search backend interprets operators within user text
factors.observable: operator behaviour from plain input

factors.name: search result authorisation
factors.def: whether per document permissions are applied by the search layer or by the caller
factors.observable: a document in results the caller may not read directly

factors.name: index staleness after deletion
factors.def: the window in which deleted content remains searchable
factors.observable: a deleted document returned by search

factors.name: aggregation as an inference channel
factors.def: whether aggregate endpoints allow filtering fine enough to isolate one record
factors.observable: a single record reconstructed from aggregates

factors.name: count and existence oracle
factors.def: whether counts reveal records the caller cannot read
factors.observable: a count differing from the filtered list

factors.name: sort and filter parameter allow list
factors.def: whether sortable and filterable fields are enumerated or taken from the request
factors.observable: sorting by an undeclared field

factors.name: pagination consistency under writes
factors.def: whether a cursor stays stable when the underlying set changes mid-walk
factors.observable: a record skipped or repeated across pages

factors.name: object storage key predictability
factors.def: whether object keys are guessable, which turns private buckets into listings
factors.observable: an object retrieved by constructing a key

factors.name: object storage listing permission
factors.def: whether list is separated from get, which decides whether names can be enumerated
factors.observable: a listing returned without explicit grant

factors.name: signed URL scope and lifetime
factors.def: what a presigned URL permits and for how long
factors.observable: a signed URL used for an operation it should not allow

factors.name: object metadata trust
factors.def: whether content type is taken from stored metadata or the bytes
factors.observable: an object served as a type it is not

factors.name: backup accessibility
factors.def: whether a backup is network reachable and whether it is encrypted at rest
factors.observable: a backup readable from the network

factors.name: export path authorisation
factors.def: whether bulk export applies the same per record checks as the UI
factors.observable: an export containing records the caller may not read

factors.name: import path validation
factors.def: whether an import validates every row and every reference
factors.observable: an imported row violating a rule the UI enforces

factors.name: restore path privilege
factors.def: whether a restore can reintroduce deleted principals or stale rights
factors.observable: a deleted principal active after a restore

factors.name: replica lag as an authorisation window
factors.def: whether a read from a lagging replica sees a stale permission decision
factors.observable: a revoked right still honoured on a replica

factors.name: transaction isolation level
factors.def: the isolation in use, which decides which anomalies are possible
factors.observable: a read anomaly consistent with a lower isolation level

factors.name: lost update on concurrent write
factors.def: whether read modify write is protected by versioning or locking
factors.observable: one of two concurrent updates silently discarded

factors.name: unique constraint versus application check
factors.def: whether uniqueness is enforced by the store, which decides races
factors.observable: a duplicate created in a race the app check should have caught

factors.name: foreign key enforcement
factors.def: whether referential integrity is enforced or left to the application
factors.observable: a child row referring to nothing

factors.name: cascade delete reach
factors.def: what a delete removes transitively, and whether that crosses tenant boundaries
factors.observable: records in another tenant removed by a cascade

factors.name: cache key tenant separation
factors.def: whether a cache key includes the tenant or principal
factors.observable: one tenant's response served to another

factors.name: cache invalidation on permission change
factors.def: whether a rights change invalidates cached responses computed under the old rights
factors.observable: a stale response carrying old permissions

factors.name: queue message trust
factors.def: whether a consumer trusts the producer and skips validation
factors.observable: a consumer acting on a message no producer should send

factors.name: queue message replay
factors.def: whether a message can be replayed and whether consumers deduplicate
factors.observable: two effects from one message

factors.name: dead letter queue exposure
factors.def: whether failed messages are readable and whether they contain secrets
factors.observable: a payload readable from a dead letter store

factors.name: queue topic authorisation
factors.def: whether publishing and subscribing are separately authorised
factors.observable: a subscription to a topic the principal should not read

factors.name: migration reversal safety
factors.def: whether a rollback discards data written since the migration
factors.observable: data loss after a rollback

factors.name: schema evolution and old client compatibility
factors.def: whether an old client can write a shape the new schema mishandles
factors.observable: a write accepted that breaks a newer reader

factors.name: encryption at rest key management
factors.def: where the key lives, who can use it, and whether it is separable from the data
factors.observable: plaintext recoverable through a data path

factors.name: field level encryption coverage
factors.def: which fields are encrypted, and whether search indexes leak them anyway
factors.observable: an encrypted field recoverable from an index

factors.name: data retention enforcement
factors.def: whether expired data is actually deleted or only flagged
factors.observable: a record past its retention window still present

factors.name: soft delete versus hard delete
factors.def: whether deleted data remains readable through admin paths
factors.observable: deleted content in an administrative view

factors.name: log and telemetry store contents
factors.def: whether request data reaches a log store with wider access than the database
factors.observable: a sensitive value in a log query result

factors.name: analytics store join key
factors.def: whether pseudonymised analytics can be rejoined to identities
factors.observable: a pseudonym resolved back to a principal

factors.name: connection string exposure
factors.def: whether credentials appear in config files, images, errors or the repo
factors.observable: a working credential in a non secret channel

factors.name: database user privilege breadth
factors.def: whether the application user can create schemas, read other databases or call filesystem functions
factors.observable: a capability beyond data manipulation

factors.name: stored procedure and function surface
factors.def: whether privileged routines are callable from the application's connection
factors.observable: a routine invoked from ordinary input

factors.name: time series and metric cardinality
factors.def: whether user supplied labels create unbounded series, a cost and probing channel
factors.observable: unbounded series growth from request labels

factors.name: file store path composition
factors.def: whether a stored path is built from user input and resolved later
factors.observable: a write outside the intended directory

factors.name: symlink and junction handling
factors.def: whether a created link can redirect a later write or read
factors.observable: a write following a link to an unintended target

factors.name: temporary file naming and location
factors.def: whether temp files are predictable and world readable
factors.observable: a readable temp artefact from another context

factors.name: archive extraction path policy
factors.def: whether extracted entry names are confined and whether symlinks are honoured
factors.observable: an extraction writing outside the target directory

factors.name: archive bomb limits
factors.def: whether expansion ratio and total size are bounded before extraction
factors.observable: expansion far beyond any stated limit

factors.name: serialisation format for cache entries
factors.def: whether cached objects are deserialised with a permissive parser
factors.observable: an object graph instantiated from a cache value

factors.name: cross region replication exposure
factors.def: whether data is replicated to a region with different legal and access rules
factors.observable: a record present in a region it was not intended for

factors.name: public snapshot or dataset residue
factors.def: whether a snapshot was ever shared publicly and whether that can be undone
factors.observable: a snapshot still reachable at its old location

factors.name: identifier reuse after deletion
factors.def: whether a deleted identifier can be reassigned, which makes old references point at new owners
factors.observable: an old reference resolving to a different record

factors.name: database version and patch level
factors.def: the running version, which selects which known behaviour applies
factors.observable: version string from a query or a header

factors.name: search index document contents
factors.def: whether the index stores full documents, which duplicates the data outside its protections
factors.observable: a full record recoverable from the index

factors.name: data lineage and provenance
factors.def: whether the origin of a record is recorded, which decides whether a poisoned import can be traced
factors.observable: a record with no traceable source
